one_sentence_story: With two dolls, a basket, a box, and one moved marble in 1985, the Sally-Anne experiment revealed how human minds around age four learn to hold someone else's outdated belief separate from reality — a skill even busy adults lose under the 'Curse of Knowledge.'
so_what_for_you: Whenever you explain an idea or resolve a misunderstanding, deliberately pause and ask: 'Did this other person actually see the marble move, or is that context only inside MY head?'

jargon_map.plain: tracking that other people hold beliefs, memories, and perspectives different from your own current knowledge
jargon_map.analogy: like keeping separate save-files for what each character in a mystery novel knows so far

jargon_map.plain: testing whether an observer predicts someone will act on their outdated belief rather than a secret change they didn't witness
jargon_map.analogy: like knowing a surprise party hides behind the door while predicting your friend expects an empty kitchen

jargon_map.plain: adult cognitive bias where knowing a fact makes it brutally hard to simulate what a newcomer doesn't know
jargon_map.analogy: like tapping a rhythm on a desk and hearing the whole orchestra in your own head

jargon_map.plain: modern finding (Milton) that communication mismatches between neurodivergent and neurotypical people stem from mutual differences in style, not a one-sided deficit
jargon_map.analogy: like two fluent speakers of different dialects needing shared translation
